title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is not a manuscript note on the divided-power de Rham complex. It is a typescript page, numbered 180 and headed 'IX', from Grothendieck's SGA 7 Exposé IX ('Modèles de Néron et monodromie'), §13.4, the complex-analytic theory. The back of the sheet was evidently reused for the handwritten notes on the neighbouring pages (Hom^d computations with the truncations τ_N of divided-power algebras S_k). The archive number 498 and the 'IX' header support this.

Mathematical content:
- Setting. There is a family of (possibly degenerating) abelian varieties, or more generally an analytic group, over a complex-analytic base S.
- Lattice and filtration. It has a lattice sheaf R (the H_1 local system) with a filtration R^t ⊂ R^f ⊂ R: the toric part and the 'fixed' part.
- Vector bundle. Put E = R ⊗_Z O_S. It carries the induced sub-bundles E^t ⊂ E^f ⊂ E and a Hodge sub-bundle F.
- Part (b), which this page concludes. The filtration induced by F on E^t is concentrated in degree -1, and the one on E/E^f in degree 0, with the degree conventions of (13.4.6). In modern terms, the graded pieces of the weight filtration W_{-2} = E^t, W_{-1} = E^f, W_0 = E have Hodge types (-1,-1) and (0,0) at the two ends.
- Part (c), the middle graded piece. Set E^ab = E^f/E^t ≅ R^ab ⊗ O_S, with R^ab = R^f/R^t. Let F^ab be the image of F^f = F ∩ E^f in E^ab. This map is injective because F ∩ E^t = 0, which is the 'first relation (*)'. Then the pair (R^ab, F^ab) is the pair (R(B), F(B)) attached to an abeloid group B over S, essentially as Lie(B)/R(B). In modern terms, Gr^W_{-1} is a polarizable variation of weight -1 Hodge structure, i.e. a family of complex tori/abelian varieties.
- Remark 13.4.18. Restricted to an open U on which R is locally constant, the statement says that (R, W, F) is an analytic family of mixed Hodge structures in Deligne's sense (Hodge II). The remark adds that this situation served as the model for Deligne's conjectures on Néron theory in higher dimension ([9, 9.8–9.13]). It then begins to note an important feature of the algebraic theory not captured here.

The page is published text; it is unrelated to the de Rham complex material on the neighbouring pages.
errors: Minor typo in the original: 'a servie de modèle' should read 'a servi de modèle'.
Notational looseness: 'B ≃ E^ab/(F^ab+R^ab)' should be read as a quotient of analytic groups/sheaves, (E^ab/F^ab)/R^ab. This is consistent with the conventions of the text and is not a real error.

ideas.what: Weight filtration E^t ⊂ E^f ⊂ E on R⊗O_S for a degenerating abelian family, with Hodge filtration types concentrated in degrees -1 and 0 at the ends
ideas.modern_name: Variation of mixed Hodge structure / 1-motive structure of the degeneration (toric, abelian and lattice parts)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA 7 IX), Deligne (Hodge II, Hodge III 1-motives)
ideas.where_published: SGA 7 I, Exposé IX, §13.4 (Lecture Notes in Math. 288, 1972)

ideas.what: Abelian part (R^ab, F^ab) defines an abeloid (complex-torus) group B over S
ideas.modern_name: Abelian part of a semi-abelian degeneration; weight -1 VHS ↔ family of complex tori

ideas.what: Remark that this analytic picture was the model for Deligne's conjectures on higher-dimensional Néron theory
ideas.modern_name: Néron models for variations of Hodge structure / admissible normal functions (Green–Griffiths–Kerr, Brosnan–Pearlstein, Schnell, Kato–Nakayama–Usui)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (conjectures), later Clemens, Saito, Green–Griffiths–Kerr, Schnell

deep.surprise_reason: This is a page of the published SGA 7 Exposé IX typescript, reused as scrap paper for the divided-power notes. Its content is in print and well known.
transcription_corrections: Page header '- 180 - IX' indicates SGA 7 Exposé IX typescript, not a manuscript note of cote 136.
R^ab, R^f, R^t are underlined (sheaf notation) throughout; the handwritten blue correction near (R^ab) is an annotation on the typescript.
'a servie' is as typed in the original (grammatical error of the source, not a transcription error).
